# otto: what the record says that is not so

## otto-L-01: "the erg at the club reads long"

Journal, 2030-02-20, `kind: claim`.

He may well be right. The point is that his own record cannot say: every
ergometer row in it came off that one machine, so there is nothing to compare
against. The claim is about a difference between two instruments and the
record contains one.

**Expected behaviour.** The engine observes that the record cannot settle the
claim and says so. It must not adjudicate by looking at his splits, because
splits off one machine cannot distinguish a fast machine from a fit rower, and
it must not quietly drop the claim either.

**What would be wrong.** Any output implying the claim was checked. It has not
been, it cannot be from this record, and a consumer that reports it as
unsupported rather than untestable has made a stronger statement than the
evidence allows.
